identity.statement: sum_{n in Z} e^{-a(n-c)^2} = sqrt(pi/a) . theta_2(-c, i pi/a), exactly, for every a > 0 and every real offset c
identity.prior_art: Poisson summation for the Gaussian; Mathlib has the same transformation un-theta'd as Complex.tsum_exp_neg_quadratic. Nothing here is new mathematics

the_discretisation_error_is_exponential.expansion: sum / integral = 1 + 2 sum_{n>=1} e^{-pi^2 n^2/a} cos(2 pi n c)
the_discretisation_error_is_exponential.consequence: the offset c enters only inside a cos multiplying an already exponentially small factor, so it is uniformly harmless — it was never the obstacle

what_this_closes_and_what_it_does_not.closes: qou-mlgp (B): the sum -> integral step in the Laplace derivation of c_sigma(4_1) = 3^{-1/4} costs only O(e^{-pi N/sqrt3}), so the one-loop constant survives it
what_this_closes_and_what_it_does_not.does_not_close: qou-mlgp (A): the Euler-Maclaurin expansion of s_k = -sum_{j<=k} log(2 sin(j pi/N)) WITH its constant. That sum has a SINGULAR integrand at the j = 0 endpoint, Poisson summation does not apply, and its corrections really are polynomial (O(log N)). See QOU/Knot/KashaevProdEndpoint.lean for the exact endpoint any refinement must hit
what_this_closes_and_what_it_does_not.still_assumed_in_lean: the Gaussian APPROXIMATION of phi near the saddle — this probe and the Lean file handle the sum of an EXACT Gaussian, not the cubic-and-higher remainder of phi
